faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: Can’t find your answer? The calculator shows every assumption and the PDF report every rate and base.

q1.q: How much is customs duty on a car from the USA?
q1.a: For passenger cars (CN 8703) duty is 10% of the CIF customs value, 22% for pickups and light trucks (8704) and 6–8% for motorcycles. Collector vehicles over 30 years old in original condition may qualify for 0%. The customs value is the purchase price plus auction fees, transport to the EU border and insurance.

q2.q: What excise applies when importing a car to Poland?
q2.a: Combustion cars up to 2000 cm³: 3.1%, above 2000 cm³: 18.6%. Hybrids: 1.55% up to 2000 cm³ and 9.3% up to 3500 cm³. Plug-in hybrids up to 2000 cm³ and electric cars are exempt. The base is the customs value plus duty, converted to PLN.

q3.q: Where is it best to clear the car: Bremerhaven, Rotterdam or Gdynia?
q3.a: Import VAT is charged by the clearance country: 19% in Germany, 21% in the Netherlands and 23% in Poland. Clearing in Germany lowers VAT, but you add a car carrier to Poland and pay excise separately at the tax office within 14 days. The calculator compares the options for your car.

q4.a: It is release with a VAT exemption in the import country when the car goes straight to a VAT-registered business in another EU state. The buyer accounts for VAT at home under the reverse charge, so it is neutral for VAT-registered companies. It is not available to private individuals.

q5.q: How long does shipping to Europe take?
q5.a: From US East Coast and Canadian ports about 2–3 weeks at sea, from California about 5 weeks, from Japan 6–7 weeks, from the UAE 3–4 weeks and from the UK a few days. Add transport from the auction yard to the port and clearance.

q6.q: Where do the exchange rates come from?
q6.a: We use NBP average rates fetched automatically every business day. Because you pay for the car days or weeks after the quote, the free range allows for currency movements.

q7.q: What does the paid PDF report include?
q7.a: Every item to the cent: auction fees by tier, transport, customs value, duty, excise and VAT with bases and rates, the list of required documents and a personal PDF to download. Pay by BLIK, card or Przelewy24.

q8.a: No. It is an estimate based on current rates and price lists. Final amounts are set by customs and the tax office, which may for example verify the customs value. The report lists all assumptions, so it is easy to compare with the official decision.

q9.a: No. We are only a calculator – we don’t buy, ship or clear cars, and we take no commission from auctions or carriers. That keeps the estimate independent. If you want, you can pass the estimate to a verified import company, but that is always your choice.

about.lead: CarImport.eu is an independent calculator of the cost of bringing a car from outside the European Union. We built it so that anyone – not just a dealer with ten years of experience – knows before buying what they will really pay.

story.title: Out of frustration with hidden costs
story.p1: A car from a US auction looks like a bargain – until you add auction fees, transport to the port, freight, duty, excise, VAT, unloading, the tow truck, translations, the roadworthiness test and registration. Each item is “small”, together they can double the price.
story.p2: The information is scattered across auction price lists, customs tariffs, exchange-rate tables and the rules of 27 countries. Broker quotes usually give one figure with no breakdown – and with their margin inside.
story.p3: We built a tool that brings it all together, calculates with current rates and shows every assumption. No sign-up, no call from a salesperson.

USA.h1: Importing a car from the USA to the EU
USA.metaTitle: Import a car from the USA to Europe – costs, duty, VAT | CarImport.eu
USA.metaDescription: How to import a car from the USA: Copart and IAAI auctions, shipping time, 10% duty, import VAT, documents and registration. Calculate the full cost in a minute.
USA.lead: The USA is the biggest source of imported cars: millions of vehicles on Copart and IAAI every year, often at prices far below the European market. Here is what the whole process looks like and what it really costs.
USA.why: Huge choice, low prices for damaged (salvage) cars, strong engines and well-equipped versions that are rare in Europe. The catch: US lighting and sometimes the speedometer must be converted, and repairs of salvage cars can be expensive.
USA.auctions: Copart and IAAI (Insurance Auto Auctions) sell mostly insurance cars with clean or salvage titles; Manheim and dealers sell cars without damage. You usually bid through a broker with an auction licence.
USA.docs: Title (clean or salvage), invoice / bill of sale, bill of lading, US export declaration (EEI/AES), customs declaration in the EU port, translations of the title and invoice, inspection certificate.
USA.tip: Check the VIN history (accidents, flood, mileage) before bidding and set aside a buffer for hidden damage – the calculator adds it as a risk scenario.

faq1.q: How long does shipping from the USA take?
faq1.a: From the East Coast (New Jersey, Savannah) about {{min}} days at sea to the North Sea ports, from Houston and California up to {{max}} days. Add 1–3 weeks for transport to the port and waiting for the vessel.

faq2.q: Is a salvage title a problem in the EU?
faq2.a: No – the EU does not use US title brands. The car must however pass the technical inspection after repairs, so budget for a proper repair and the hidden-damage risk.

CANADA.h1: Importing a car from Canada to the EU
CANADA.metaTitle: Import a car from Canada to Europe – costs, duty, VAT | CarImport.eu
CANADA.metaDescription: Import a car from Canada: Copart and IAAI Canada, shipping from Halifax and Montreal, 10% duty, VAT, documents and registration. Full cost calculator.
CANADA.lead: Canadian cars are similar to American ones but often better prepared for winter, with metric speedometers and lower prices in Canadian dollars. Shipping from Halifax and Montreal to Europe is among the shortest across the Atlantic.
CANADA.why: Metric instrument clusters, winter packages, block heaters and good rust protection; prices in CAD are often lower than in the USA for the same model.
CANADA.auctions: Copart and IAAI operate in Canada as well; dealer and private sales are an option for cars without damage. Bidding goes through a broker.
CANADA.docs: Registration / ownership (or salvage title), bill of sale, bill of lading, Canadian export declaration, EU customs declaration, translations, inspection certificate.
CANADA.tip: Eastern provinces (Ontario, Quebec) are closest to the ports of Montreal and Halifax – inland transport from the west costs much more.

faq1.q: How long does shipping from Canada take?
faq1.a: From Halifax and Montreal about {{min}}–{{max}} days at sea to the North Sea ports, plus transport to the port and waiting for the vessel.

faq2.q: Does a Canadian car need conversion?
faq2.a: Usually less than a US car: the speedometer is already metric. Lighting (amber rear indicators, side markers) may still need adapting to EU rules.

JAPAN.h1: Importing a car from Japan to the EU
JAPAN.metaTitle: Import a car from Japan to Europe – JDM costs, duty, VAT | CarImport.eu
JAPAN.metaDescription: Import a JDM car from Japan: USS auctions, auction sheets, shipping from Yokohama, duty, VAT, right-hand drive and registration. Full cost calculator.
JAPAN.lead: Japan is the home of JDM cars: low mileage, excellent condition and models never sold in Europe. Auction sheets describe every car in detail – but the cars are right-hand drive and the journey is long.
JAPAN.why: Very good condition thanks to strict inspections (shaken), honest auction grading and unique sports and kei cars. Prices in yen are attractive.
JAPAN.auctions: USS is the largest auction network; others include TAA, CAA and JU. You buy through an exporter who translates the auction sheet and handles export deregistration.
JAPAN.docs: Export certificate (deregistration), auction sheet and invoice, bill of lading, EU customs declaration, translations, inspection certificate.
JAPAN.tip: Check whether your country restricts right-hand-drive cars and how the inspection treats them before you buy.

faq1.q: How long does shipping from Japan take?
faq1.a: Via the Suez Canal about {{min}}–{{max}} days at sea depending on the EU port – Mediterranean ports are the fastest. Add the time for export documents.

faq2.q: Can I register a right-hand-drive car?
faq2.a: In most EU countries yes, sometimes with headlight adjustment. A few countries limit RHD cars for permanent registration – check your local rules before buying.

UAE.h1: Importing a car from Dubai (UAE) to the EU
UAE.metaTitle: Import a car from Dubai (UAE) to Europe – costs, duty, VAT | CarImport.eu
UAE.metaDescription: Import a car from Dubai and the UAE: Emirates Auction and dealers, GCC spec, shipping from Jebel Ali, duty, VAT and registration. Full cost calculator.
UAE.lead: Dubai is a market of premium and sports cars with low mileage, often barely used. GCC-spec cars are built for heat and sold at attractive prices.
UAE.why: Luxury and sports models, low mileage and dry climate (no rust). Prices in dirhams are pegged to the US dollar.
UAE.auctions: Emirates Auction and dealers in Dubai and Sharjah; a local exporter arranges the export certificate and shipping from Jebel Ali.
UAE.docs: Export certificate, invoice, bill of lading, EU customs declaration, translations, inspection certificate.
UAE.tip: Heat wears rubber parts and interiors – ask for photos of seals, tyres and dashboard.

faq1.q: How long does shipping from Dubai take?
faq1.a: From Jebel Ali through Suez about {{min}}–{{max}} days at sea depending on the EU port; Mediterranean ports are the closest.

faq2.a: A car built for the Gulf market: stronger cooling and air conditioning, sometimes different emissions equipment. It can be registered in the EU after the technical inspection.

UK.h1: Importing a car from the UK to the EU
UK.metaTitle: Import a car from the UK after Brexit – costs, duty, VAT | CarImport.eu
UK.metaDescription: Import a car from the UK after Brexit: customs duty and preferential origin, VAT, right-hand drive, short shipping and registration. Full cost calculator.
UK.lead: Since Brexit a car from the United Kingdom is an import from outside the EU: customs declaration, duty and import VAT apply. The journey is short, and cars made in the UK or the EU may qualify for 0% duty.
UK.why: A large used-car market, good service histories and short shipping by RoRo or ferry. Right-hand drive needs to be considered.
UK.auctions: Copart UK, BCA, Manheim UK and dealers. Buying from a VAT-registered dealer means the UK VAT can be refunded on export.
UK.docs: V5C logbook, invoice, export declaration, preferential origin statement (for 0% duty), EU customs declaration, translations, inspection certificate.
UK.tip: Ask the seller for a statement of preferential origin – under the EU–UK trade agreement it can cut the duty to zero for cars made in the UK or the EU.

faq1.q: How long does transport from the UK take?
faq1.a: Only {{min}}–{{max}} days by sea (RoRo or ferry), plus customs formalities on both sides.

faq2.q: Do I pay duty on a car from the UK?
faq2.a: Yes, 10% – unless the car has proven preferential origin (made in the UK or the EU) under the EU–UK agreement, in which case duty can be 0%. Import VAT is always due.

country.h1: {{country}}: importing a car from outside the EU
country.metaTitle: {{country}} – car import: VAT {{vat}}%, registration, ports | CarImport.eu
country.metaDescription: Importing a car into {{country}} from the USA, Canada, Japan, the UAE or the UK: import VAT {{vat}}%, registration, inspection, nearest ports and the full cost.
country.lead: Everything that matters when you register an imported car in {{country}}: tax, authorities, inspection and the cheapest ports.
country.p1: Customs duty is the same in every EU country: 10% of the CIF value for passenger cars. Import VAT is paid in the country where the car is cleared – {{vat}}% if you clear it here.
country.p2: Clearing in another EU country with lower VAT can be cheaper even with the extra transport – the calculator compares all ports door to door.
country.p3: Local registration taxes and inspections are not harmonised in the EU; plan their cost and time before you buy.
country.portsNote: Estimated road distance to the population centre of {{country}}.

faq1.q: How much VAT do I pay on an imported car?
faq1.a: If the car is cleared in {{country}}, {{vat}}% of the customs value plus duty and transport costs to the destination. Clearing elsewhere in the EU means that country’s import VAT.

faq2.q: Where do I register an imported car?
faq2.a: At {{authority}}, after the inspection ({{inspection}}) and with translated purchase and customs documents.

port.h1: Port of {{port}} ({{country}}): customs clearance of imported cars
port.metaDescription: Clearing an imported car in {{port}} ({{country}}): terminal and agent fees, import VAT {{vat}}%, sailing times from the USA, Japan and the UAE, distances.
port.lead: {{port}} is a port of clearance in {{country}}. Here are its fees, sailing times and road distances – and whether it is worth clearing your car here.
port.sailingNote: Shared container from the main export ports; RoRo takes a few days longer.
port.p1: Clearing in {{port}} means paying import VAT of {{country}} ({{vat}}%). If you register the car in another EU country, the car is then delivered by road.
port.p2: The calculator compares {{port}} with all other EU ports for your address and shows the cheapest option.

faq1.q: How much does clearing a car in {{port}} cost?
faq1.a: Terminal handling and devanning about {{unloading}}, customs agent about {{agency}}, plus customs duty and import VAT of {{vat}}%.

faq2.q: Can I clear a car here and register it in another EU country?
faq2.a: Yes. A private buyer pays the import VAT here; a VAT-registered company can use customs procedure 4200 and account for VAT in its own country.
